correctness.rationale: With n=2m+1 odd, one s->t delegation changes majority correctness only in the two pivotal cases S=m-1,t correct,s incorrect (gain) and S=m,t incorrect,s correct (loss), where S is the number of correct votes among 2m-1 ordinary conditionally independent voters. Their equal central binomial coefficients give exact Δ_m=binom(2m-1,m-1) Σ_b π_b [(1-q_b)c_b(1-a_b)-q_b a_b(1-c_b)] [q_b(1-q_b)]^(m-1). A positive exponential normalization yields a monotone affine exponential ratio, so across integer m there is at most one sign reversal, even if a coefficient vanishes or λ0=λ1. Statewise gain criterion follows by dividing positive odds factors. With a=(3/5,3/5), c=(4/5,4/5), q=(3/5,4/5), π=(1/3,2/3), direct exact fractions Δ_1=-1/375, Δ_2=2/625 and Δ_m>0 thereafter. Independently compared complete Bernoulli outcome enumeration with pivotal formula for n=3,5,7,9, including Δ_3=248/46875 and Δ_4=56/9375. All-size result is the pivotal partition, not finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Gilbert, Schmid, Schnell, Svoboda and Yeo (arXiv:2608.16738) study the same two-state common-signal liquid democracy model and related competence-versus-accuracy effects, making it the decisive comparison. Their indexed claims focus on general mechanisms, correlations and asymptotic/other delegation architectures, whereas the present theorem gives fixed-edge finite-population two-exponential sign geometry. Their full primary text could not be re-read in this run; an authorized access attempt returned disconnected institutional VPN. Kahng–Mackenzie–Procaccia (2021) use scalar independent competences and cannot express two-state competition; Abramowitz–Mattei (2024) compare to a different benchmark. Resultary query returned unrelated voting-rule census findings rather than an identical single-edge conditional gain theorem. Originality remains a qualified best-of-knowledge PASS; plausible known pivotal-identity reductions are a specific risk.

No assertion for strategic edge selection, more than two states, or heterogeneous backgrounds growing with n.

value.rationale: The single edge is the elementary action in correlated epistemic liquid voting. The exact conditional cost/benefit criterion and at-most-one population reversal resolve a natural sensitivity question as electorate size varies. The sharp three-to-five reversal even when delegate competence dominates in BOTH states is an informative structural counterexample to naive competence monotonicity; no broad equilibrium mechanism is claimed.
